name: Precision
rationale: White and pale steel with a single diagnostic navy for every action and link. A signal vermilion appears only as a tick or marker (the wordmark drop, the active section bar, the flagship rule, the workflow start, the ICMR badge dot) and never carries text. Cool, exact and instrument-like: the colours of a datasheet.

name: Daybreak
rationale: Warm ivory and a deeper oat for alternating bands, with a deep bronze-gold carrying every button and link so the warm scheme still passes AA. The amber-gold is strictly decorative: the sunrise glow, the arc, the half-sun arches and the drop. Light and optimistic without tipping into a wellness palette.

name: Molecular
rationale: Indigo-violet on white, with a probe cyan reserved for markers — the drop, a node, the guides on Figure 2. The violet is dark enough to carry body-weight links and diagram strokes at AA, so the figures can be drawn in the primary rather than in grey, which is what makes them read as drafted rather than decorative.

name: Field & Lab
rationale: Earthy off-white and sand grounds with a warm-charcoal primary, so the interface recedes and the photographs supply the colour. Terracotta is reserved for markers, rules and the drop. A documentary palette for a supplier whose evidence is its field and laboratory work.

name: Assurance
rationale: Medical teal on a mint ground with white cards, darkened from the database's #0891B2 so every action passes AA. Aqua is the light motif and stays decorative — check seals, rules, the drop. Calm and clinical: the register of a manufacturer whose claims can be checked.

name: Lumen
rationale: The database's Biotech / Life Sciences scheme — DNA blue and life green on an ice-white ground — with the sky blue darkened to AA for every action and the emerald kept as a decorative glow. Luminous rather than bright: daylight through a clean instrument window.

name: Canopy
rationale: Deep nature green with a sparing sun-amber mark on leaf-white, the closest of the eight to the company's own green and amber. Ink and footer are deep green too, so the page reads as one material. The amber is used only for the drop, the sun disc and small markers.

name: Civic
rationale: Slate-black on white with a single blue for links and actions, the highest-contrast palette of the eight: every text pair clears 7:1. No colour carries meaning on its own — tags and states are marked with text and borders as well — so the page survives a bright phone screen outdoors.

name: Brief green
rationale: Reference palette from website-info.md §5, not tied to a layout: white and warm off-white grounds, near-black text, deep brand green and an amber-gold 'light' motif, so every layout can be judged in the company's existing colours. The green is the brief's approximate #1E6B4E and should be re-sampled from the logo once the SVG arrives.

name: Brand Classic
rationale: Taken strictly from the logo. Primary is the leaf green of the mark (#6B9D2A, 3.24:1 on white) moved one step down its own ramp to #527E15 so it passes AA; accent is the sun gold #FFC80C at its exact logo value, decorative only; ink is the logo's own figure colour #252820; the pale leaf tint, muted and line are the same green hue at very low chroma, so even the greys carry the brand.

name: Brand Light
rationale: The same two logo hues, pushed lighter and softer: a warm off-white made from the sun gold at near-zero chroma, the palest leaf tint for alternate bands, a softened green-grey ink, and the leaf green at its 700 step (#40640B, 6.67:1) reserved for calls to action and key figures. The accent is the sun gold lifted to its 300 tint for the hero glow and small markers only.

name: Evaluation
rationale: The brief's deep green carries every action and nothing else, on white and a barely-green off-white; amber appears once, as the rule beside the company description. Near-black ink with tabular figures keeps the page reading like a specification file rather than a campaign.

name: Oxblood
rationale: A dried-blood oxide red for every action, taken from the specimen the product is built around, on warm paper and a deeper oat for alternating bands. Amber is decorative only. Warm enough to sit beside field photography, dark enough to pass AA comfortably on both grounds.

name: Graphite & Sun
rationale: Graphite and white with a warm-grey panel colour, so photographs and figures carry the page. The logo's sun gold is the only hue, used for small markers and rules and never behind text. The register of an instrument maker's product page.
